concurrency_selection.reasoning: Verified from real data across all seven runs: exactly 4 LLM-eligible agents exist per ticker, always. Agent-level concurrency=4 therefore gives every independent agent its own dedicated worker -- concurrency 6 and 8 were simulated and produce IDENTICAL stage makespan to 4 in every single run (there is nothing left to parallelize past the 4th lane). This is not a case of 'diminishing returns past 4' -- it is ZERO further returns past 4, cleanly proven by the fan-out shape itself, not merely inferred. C4 also reuses the exact same value already proven safe against the real Provider for alpha_classifier and evidence_stance_classifier, rather than a new ceiling.
concurrency_selection.c2_vs_c4_comparison: C4 offers a LARGE incremental benefit over C2, not a small one -- confirmed in every run (46-50% further stage-time reduction from C2 to C4; QQQ post-fix: C2=324.6s -> C4=167.0s, a further 48.6% reduction). Section 15's 'prefer C2 if C4 offers only a small incremental gain' condition does NOT apply here -- C4 is clearly, substantially better than C2 across the whole seven-run set.

provider_pressure_analysis.expected_simultaneous_requests: Up to 4 concurrent structured_adapter batch requests, potentially overlapping with alpha_classifier's own independent pool of up to 4 and evidence_stance_classifier's own independent pool of up to 4 -- these three pools are independent, uncoordinated ThreadPoolExecutors. Worst-case combined simultaneous Provider load across all three tasks, if their execution windows happened to overlap, could reach 12. In practice these three tasks run as SEQUENTIAL PIPELINE STAGES within one research run (structured_adapter completes before alpha_classifier begins, which completes before evidence_stance_classifier begins -- confirmed in B1's own stage-sequencing analysis), so true simultaneous cross-task overlap is not expected in the normal pipeline flow.
provider_pressure_analysis.worst_case_retry_concurrency: Retries do not multiply concurrency -- each agent's own batches perform their own bounded retry loops independently; a batch mid-retry still counts as exactly one in-flight slot.
provider_pressure_analysis.why_the_cap_is_reasonable: 4 matches the real fan-out shape exactly (4 agents), matches the already-proven cap for the other two concurrent tasks, and going higher (6/8) is proven to add zero further benefit while only adding unvalidated Provider pressure for no reason.

concurrency_selection.granularity_tradeoff_disclosed: The TRUE, finest-grained independent unit is the (agent, batch) pair (8 total for QQQ post-fix, since 2 of the 4 agents' reports need 2 batches each). Batch-level flattening (parallelizing all 8 across a shared worker pool) was simulated and shows a marginally BETTER or comparable result to agent-level in most runs (e.g. QQQ post-fix batch-level C4=173.5s vs agent-level C4=167.0s -- agent-level is actually fractionally BETTER here due to how the specific per-run durations happen to bin-pack; this is not a general guarantee, just what this measured dataset shows). Agent-level concurrency was CHOSEN for implementation specifically because it requires ZERO changes to adapt_raw_agent_outputs/_llm_batch_enrichment (the well-tested functions with 124 existing passing tests), whereas true batch-level flattening would require refactoring those functions' internals to expose their own batch loop externally -- a materially larger, higher-risk implementation surface for, on this evidence, no measured latency benefit. This is a deliberate 'implementation simplicity' tradeoff, one of the five explicit selection criteria, not an oversight.

seven_run_scheduling_simulation.method: Same greedy list-scheduling simulation as Slice 2A (a min-heap of C worker free-at times), applied at BOTH the true batch-level granularity (for reference/comparison) and the CHOSEN agent-level granularity (summing each agent's own batches into one work-item duration) using each run's own persisted structured_adapter call latencies.
seven_run_scheduling_simulation.diminishing_returns: At the agent level, C4 == C6 == C8 in EVERY single run (confirmed, not estimated) -- there are only 4 independent lanes, so any concurrency cap above 4 is provably a complete no-op for this task. C2->C4 is NOT a diminishing-returns zone (46-50% further reduction in every run) -- the returns diminish sharply and completely only immediately AFTER C4.
